en: The Recorded Sayings of Master Mian, Compiled by His Disciples Chongyue and Liaowu and Others. The Recorded Sayings of Master Mian during his tenure at Qianming Chan Monastery on Mount Wugu in Western Quzhou.
Compiled by his junior disciples Chongyue and Liaowu.
On the first day of the eighth month in the third year of the Qiandao era,
the Master accepted the invitation at this monastery and ascended the seat, saying:
Just now, before the drums had even sounded,
he was called Zen Master Jie;
but now that he has ascended the seat, [he is no longer so].
To call him "Elder Wugu" is to abruptly change his name and alter his title;
he is one who wears fur and bears horns.
Dragging plows and pulling harrows,
they sink and surface within the realms of other species.
Since the debt of karma is difficult to evade,
one must joyfully endure it;
seeing through it in this way, one attains thorough penetration.
The new elder has finished his work in the world;
had it not been so, Elder Jie would have lost ground today.
The expression of gratitude is not recorded.
Again, he raised the Way of the Three Sages:
"Whenever I encounter a person, I manifest it."
When I go out, I do not act for the sake of others to promote the Way;
when I encounter people, I do not come forth.
When he emerged, he immediately became a person.
Later, Master Baiyun Yuan commented:
"These two venerable seniors..."
Each has its own point of impact.
Now tell me:
which one comes first?
"Which one is behind?
The Master called to the assembly, saying,
"Master Baiyun ended up using the wrong terminology."
Little do they realize that these two venerable masters did not even reach the village.
Since then, the matter has not been resolved;
it continues right up to the present day,
becoming nothing but a subject of idle gossip.
Why? Because after a character has been transcribed three times, the "crow" (wu) becomes a "horse" (ma).
Descend from your seat.
He entered the abbot’s quarters,
took his seat, and said,
"This room is profoundly deep and vast."
It cannot be reached by either speech or silence.
Layman Vimalakīrti was just now obstructing this very point;
his words were still drowsy and he had not yet awakened.
When the Seventh Patriarch arrived,
his defeat was even more complete;
Master Jie’s mouth was like a beggar’s tattered rice bag.
"And how is it established?
He let out a shout and said,
"Without entering the great waves."
"Vying to see those who play amidst the surging tide.
On the twenty-second day of the eighth month,
he opened the hall for formal teaching at this monastery.
The offering for the consecration of the Buddha has concluded.
Again, holding up incense, he says:
"This one portion of incense..."
It has been gathered for a long time;
the more one seeks to conceal it, the more it is revealed.
Today, humans and devas have assembled from all quarters.
I cannot help but explain it from the beginning.
In years past, after returning from my travels in Jiangxi,
I intended to go to Siming.
Just as he was about to reach Zhi-er of Wuzhou,
bystanders and brothers mistakenly pointed out the wrong path.
He burst into Mount Mingguo in Quzhou and saw an old monk there,
looking utterly disheveled and unkempt.
This was far too extreme and did not accord with human feeling;
having already gone wrong, he followed the error by performing three prostrations,
which has continued down to the present day.
It is too late for regret.
Nevertheless, as it is said:
"An offense has its source; a debt has its owner."
I burn incense in this burner as an offering to the Eighteenth Generation Abbot Ying’an Dashi, who resided at Mount Tiantong in his final years,
in order to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.
Thereupon, he adjusted his robes and took his seat.
After the exchange of questions and answers was concluded, he said:
The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs resembles the mechanism of an iron ox:
when it departs, it is immediately sealed.
Abiding is itself the breaking of the seal.
The myriad phenomena of the universe—
light and dark, form and emptiness— are all thus.
Sentient and insentient beings are sealed by a single seal;
there is not even a hair’s breadth of leakage.
There is not even a hair’s breadth of wandering activity;
there is not even a hair’s breadth of arising or ceasing;
there is not even a hair’s breadth of movement or agitation.
It is like gold being compared to gold,
or water being compared to water;
all external conditions are utterly severed.
Transcending all realms of existence,
the Sage lives by means of this longevity;
thus his life is as eternal as Heaven and Earth.
If one uses this to bless a worthy governor,
then Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou used it to bring peace and joy to the people.
By this, may the world be brought peace and prosperity;
by this, may the Great Teaching be propagated;
by this, may the True Lineage be upheld.
Nevertheless, even so, tell me:
where is the seal right now?
"Where is it? After a long silence, he struck his whisk and said:
"The hawk-bow hangs high; the smoke of war has ceased."
The ten thousand nations sing songs of joy in the peace of the age.
Again, Baoshou ascends the hall for the opening of the dharma assembly;
the Three Sages push forward a monk.
Baoshou struck him.
Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher in this manner,
you will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhinzhou."
Baoshou cast down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The Master said,
"Those two venerable elders."
"It is indeed beautiful,
but if one wishes to uphold the true lineage of Linji,
each person still lacks one blow of the staff."
Furthermore, tell me:
where is his deficiency?
Those who possess the eye of discernment [should know].
Try to settle this and observe.
Entering the hall, he said:
"The Buddha taught all dharmas."
To deliver all minds,
I have no mind at all;
what use have I for any phenomena?
Since there is neither mind nor phenomena,
the mountains, rivers, and the great earth [are all empty].
From where does it come?
What are these things that see, hear, perceive, and know?
He then let out a shout and said:
"To gaze at the water's edge from the brink of a cliff—
this will surely cause a groundless bout of sorrow."
Ascending the hall:
one step forward, one step back;
one movement, one stillness.
One must believe that the Nāga is always in meditative concentration;
seizing and releasing,
killing and giving life.
In all four directions and eight facets, the talk flows freely;
the Great Elephant of Jiazhou eats too much salt,
and the Iron Ox of Shanyu grows ever thirstier.
"If you engage in speculative deliberation regarding the Buddha-dharma,
the day will come when you eat iron rods.
[He] ascended the hall.
"Knowing it as an illusion is itself detachment;
no further expedient means are required.
With these words, he struck once with the whisk on the left side.
Realize it right here.
To leave illusion is itself awakening;
there is no gradual process.
Striking once with the whisk on the right side, he says:
"Receive this here.
When one person gives rise to the true and returns to the source,"
"The empty space of the ten directions shall all vanish away.
(With the whisk, he draws a single stroke across the middle.)
Receive it right here.
All of Wugu’s entanglements have been thoroughly seen through by everyone.
The nostrils and eyes of all people have been pierced through by the whisk of Wugu;
for what reason do they fail to perceive it and remain unaware?
Among them, perhaps one or two may suddenly realize their error;
yet even so, the black lacquered staff has not yet been let go.
Why? Because the waves of Caoqi are just like those [of the sea];
countless ordinary people are submerged and drowned upon the land.
Ascending the hall,
a monk asked:
"What was the meaning behind Deshan’s carrying of the alms bowl?"
The Master said,
"There is no meaning or intent.
The student stepped forward and asked:
"Why do you go down to the Sangha hall for alms?
The Master said,
"If I wish to walk, I walk."
When it was time to sit, he sat;
then he cited the Venerable Xuefeng, who addressed the assembly, saying:
"To gather up the entire great earth..."
"As large as a grain of millet,
it is tossed before one's face;
the lacquer bucket does not understand."
"Strike the drum and call for all to look!
The Master said,
"This old fellow!"
He ascended Mount Touzi three times and visited Dongshan nine times,
exhausting every stratagem.
In the end, he went back to the Aoshan Inn and,
making no compromise,
let out a cry, saying:
Today is the beginning of the completion of the Way at Mount Ao.
Today is the beginning of the completion of the Way at Mount Ao.
[He] then took all people and things of the great earth.
Making it for one's own personal use causes the ancestral tradition to be insulted beneath the thousand peaks.
Wugu’s announcement in this manner was not intended to suppress Xuefeng; rather,
it was meant for the sake of the patch-robed monks throughout the world.
Henceforth, each of you shall have your own path;
do not all collectively harbor the deluded views of a wild fox spirit. *A shout.*
Descending from the seat.
On the occasion of the Sacred Festival, he ascends the hall.
The Mahāyāna Dharma.
Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations,
where the Buddhas' teachings cannot reach—
hold the whisk well!
He then raised his whisk and said,
"Do you see it? With this,
I offer my congratulations on your longevity."
His lifespan is equal to Mount Sumeru.
Entering the hall, he raised the topic:
"The World-Honored One was at the assembly on Vulture Peak."
Five hundred bhikṣus attained the four dhyānas and were endowed with the five supernormal powers.
Not yet having attained the patience of the Dharma (dharmanidhyānaksānti),
they each saw [the Buddha] for themselves through the supernormal power of knowledge of past lives (pūrvanivāsajñānābhijñā).
Past acts of killing one's father or mother,
as well as other grave offenses,
[are to be purified] within one's own mind.
Each harbors doubts regarding the profound Dharma and is unable to enter into its realization.
Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority,
then took a sharp sword in his hand and held it threateningly toward the Tathāgata.
The World-Honored One said to Mañjuśrī, "Stop, stop!
You must not commit such an act of rebellion. Do not harm me!"
"I shall certainly be harmed;
I am being harmed for doing good, Mañjuśrī."
From the very beginning, there has been no self or person;
yet when thoughts arise within the mind,
the "self" is inevitably harmed.
This is precisely what is called "harming.
Thereupon, the five hundred bhikṣus realized their own original minds.
It is like a dream and like an illusion.
Within dreams and illusions,
there is no self and no person.
Even unto the parents who gave birth to him;
then, five hundred bhikṣus praised him in unison, saying:
Mañjuśrī, the Great Sage of Wisdom,
has profoundly penetrated the very source and depths of the Dharma;
with his own hand, he grasps a sharp sword.
Holding it, he presses against the body of the Tathāgata;
as with the sword, so too is the Buddha.
They are of one mark, without duality.
It is signless and unarisen;
how can there be killing within this?
The Master said:
If one acts for others, one must act to the very end;
if one kills, one must see the blood.
Mañjuśrī exhausted every ounce of strength from his wrists.
For now, one does not know where this sword came from;
it brings misfortune upon the Old Śākyamuni, who,
though possessed of a mouth all over his body, cannot even begin to explain it away.
If five hundred bhikṣus were to attain enlightenment in such a manner,
they would enter hell as swiftly as an arrow shot;
it would be as if they had suddenly overturned the great ocean.
He topples Mount Sumeru over.
Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the Brahma Heaven,
striking Indra right on the tip of his nose.
When a carp from the Eastern Sea is struck with a single blow,
the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
How, then, do you deliberate upon this?
After a long silence, he said:
"Since I first mastered the Three Platforms dance, every beat has been nothing but song. He then ascended the hall.
Using a wedge to extract a wedge becomes a mere conventional path;
transmitting mind by means of mind [is likewise so].
Seeing that the illness was deepening,
Daruma did not understand the direct, head-on phrase;
instead, he went to Mount Song.
Facing the wall for nine years;
later generations of descendants have inherited the void and echoed the resonance.
Raising an eyebrow, blinking an eye,
administering a blow, or shouting "Ho!"—
all these are but yellow leaves used to stop a child's crying.
When Wugu reached this point,
he was truly left with no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth.
Biting down on his teeth,
he joins with all of you in mixing mud and water.
He strikes the meditation staff once and says:
Unless one has endured the piercing cold to the very bone,
how can one obtain the fragrance of the plum blossoms that strikes the nose?
Descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall because of the snow:
Everywhere before one’s eyes, the falling flakes present auspicious snow;
filling the gullies and blocking the ravines, who can discern it?
Mañjuśrī has nowhere to suddenly hide his whole body;
Samantabhadra has lost the true, wondrous secret.
The crow has transformed into a white-headed crow.
The iron tree is turned into silver threads entwined.
I ask all you people: do you perceive it or not?
Not a single person stands in the courtyard for even a moment.
"This is precisely the season of Great Peace.
With a shout,
he descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall,
[the Master] raised an ancient precedent: "In the past,
there was a woman who supported a master of a hermitage."
For twenty years,
he constantly had a young woman deliver food and attend to his needs.
One day, he had a woman embrace him firmly and asked,
"At this very moment, how is it?
The Master said:
A withered tree leans against a cold cliff;
for three winters there has been no warmth.
The woman returned and reported this to her grandmother.
Poyun said,
"For twenty years,
I have been able to provide for nothing but this worldly fellow."
He then set fire to and burned down the hut.
The Master said,
"This is a public case."
In the monastic community, there are few who can truly bring this up or address it.
Old Monk Jie has torn his own face open,
yet he cannot avoid suffering a defeat once more.
He also called for everyone from all quarters to examine this,
and then addressed the assembly, saying:
"This old woman!"
The inner chamber is deep and secure,
impenetrable as a sealed vessel;
yet he scatters flowers upon the withered tree.
Flames burst forth from within the cold crags;
this monk stands solitary and towering,
accustomed to entering the surging waves.
Casually sitting, he cuts off the surging tide;
in the end, his body is not wet by so much as a drop of water.
If one examines this closely, [one sees it is thus].
As for "beating the shackles and striking the chains," there are indeed these two people; however,
as for the Buddha-dharma...
It has not yet been seen even in a dream.
Wugu held it up in this manner;
ultimately, where does its meaning lead?
After a long silence, he said:
"A single skein of green silk cannot be gathered;
it is draped with mist upon the jade balustrade."
Ascending the hall, he said:
"There is a thing prior to heaven and earth;
formless, it is fundamentally still and silent."
Able to serve as the lord of the myriad phenomena, not withering along with the four seasons.
Now tell me: how is this so?
"What kind of thing is it?
A certain fellow without nostrils immediately said,
"It cannot be captured even by a brush."
It is like a painting that can never be finished;
even with the Buddha-eye one cannot see it.
It is neither recognized nor known.
Such a theoretical discourse is precisely what is called "a single phrase that hits the mark."
Ten thousand kalpas of tethering posts for donkeys—
Wugū has a single saying that does not serve to support the school or establish the teaching.
Furthermore, I must strip away the flesh-bound undershirt of all the monks in the world.
Everyone, you must listen with utmost attention.
After a long silence, he said:
"The spoon is good for scooping rice;
the chopsticks are good for poking."
Vegetarian meal followed by a formal lecture.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: A monk asked Liangshan.
"How is it when a domestic thief is difficult to guard against?
Sanshan said,
"If you recognize him, he cannot be an enemy."
The monk asked,
"What is it like after one has recognized it?
Shanshan said:
He was demoted to the realm of non-arising.
A monk asked,
"Is this not the place where he establishes his body and sustains his life?"
Shan said,
"Dead water does not harbor dragons.
A monk asked, "..."
"What is the living water dragon?
The Master said,
"It raises clouds but does not spit mist."
The monk said,
"What is it like when, all of a sudden, the torrents of rain pour down and the mountains topple over?
The Master seized him by his sitting mat on the mountain slope and held him fast.
"And do not get the corner of this old monk’s cassock wet.
The Master called to the assembly, saying,
"The old thief of Liangshan!"
Compassion is excessive.
He gives the thief a ladder and leads him into the house.
Exhausting one's family wealth and raising a great clamor,
yet failing to sever the life-root of others.
This causes the thieving mind not to die out.
If it were Wugu, he would not have acted this way.
Suppose someone were to ask: "When a domestic thief is difficult to guard against, what should one do?"
He simply cuts it off with a single stroke,
teaching him to be free and unencumbered,
making him a "white-handed" thief.
They raid camps and plunder outposts everywhere.
Suddenly, he picks up his staff and says:
"This whole crew of bandits!"
"What are you seeking here?
he said, as he descended from his seat and drove everyone away at once.
Then he ascended the hall.
Citing a verse by Layman Pang:
"The ten directions gather together as one.

"An iron wall, a silver mountain;
everyone studies non-action.
The Master said:
The sun and moon shine upon it;
this is the field for selecting Buddhas.
The Master said:
Dragons and snakes are intermingled;
with an empty mind, one returns having passed the imperial examination.
The Master said:
Ordinary people and sages dwell together.
Suddenly picking up his staff and holding it crosswise, he said:
"Pang Jushi is sitting right here."
"Do you all see this?
He then threw down his staff and said,
"Three lifetimes, sixty kalpas."
Ascending the hall, he raised an old case:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when there has been long rain and no clearing?
Yunmen replied, "Zha. (A sharp, piercing sound.)
The Master said:
"O Great Assembly!
Yunmen’s single stroke."
The heavens are vast and all-encompassing;
the waters of the sea surge with waves;
Mount Sumeru rises towering and majestic.
Suddenly picking up his staff and striking it once,
he said: "Master Yunmen had no place here to draw breath."
Now tell me:
where is Wugu’s living eye?

Then the rain suddenly cleared;
the heavens were bright and the earth was tranquil.
Hanshan clapped his hands.
Shide was joyful.
To understand it in such a way is like driving a nail into dry land.
When Vice Minister Li entered the mountain, he ascended the hall.
A hidden bird’s cry shattered the *nāga*-samādhi;
immediately, the star of literature was seen entering the temple.
He hurriedly stepped out his sandals to welcome him with a smiling face;
ascending the forest springs, he awakened the wind and thunder.
Where the wind and thunder arise—
The myriad peaks give birth to spring;
the true eye is clearly illuminated;
throughout the ten voids, there is no interval.
In hand, he carries the sun and moon of Zhongni;
at his waist, he wears the numinous talisman of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Wherever he is, he brings forth auspicious omens and blessings.
He serves as a tortoise-shell and a mirror;
he constitutes a rampart and a moat for the Dharma-gate,
and acts as a pillar and a limb for the royal house.
This is not the wondrous application of supernormal powers,
nor is it the natural state of things as they are. Why is this so?
Since I have severed the path of a thousand differences,
I walk upon the crown of Vairocana.
[Ascending the hall.]
"The very mind is Buddha;
the iron ox has no bones.
Neither mind nor Buddha."
The empty mountain rises abruptly:
it is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.
A person comes from Chenzhou.
I have received news from Xuzhou,
reporting that this year’s silkworms and wheat have ripened,
and the winds and rains have been timely.
The five grains were abundant and the myriad people were joyful.
When the old man Wang Lao of East Village heard this, he said: [he had obtained it].
Laughing and singing, he said:
"From of old, I have never sung a song of empty deception;
I carry fire to burn the mountains and gather marsh snails from the fields."
A fish-fan atop a white-boned tree;
a bird builds its nest on a rapids.
Good assembly!

The Master said,
"Ultimately, where do you establish yourself and settle your life?

opening the clouds of my delusion and enabling me to enter.

Reflecting back, the luminous realm is like a rushing torrent;
if one can recognize the meaning within it,
one will cut off all manifold distinctions at their source.

as if at ease yet not at ease.

he voids excrement and urine within the abbot’s quarters;
with eyes wide open, he utters mad ravings and delirious speech.

At this very moment,
if someone can save you, [it will be done].

King Yama is not your father.

in the fourth year of the Chunxi era, he...
An imperial decree was issued for him to reside at Mount Jing;
he was summoned to face the Emperor in Xuande Hall,
where he was questioned on the essential tenets of the Buddha-dharma.
When he opened the hall at Lingyin,
the Emperor again dispatched an imperial messenger to bestow incense;
monks and laypeople gathered to watch like a wall.
In the seventh year, he moved from Mount Jing to Lingyin.
The Emperor personally inscribed a calligraphic edict and inquired of him regarding the essentials of the Dharma.
He further dispatched an attendant official to inquire about the "four illnesses" mentioned in the *Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*.
The Master answered each question with truthful words.
He was treated with profound favor and honor.
In the eleventh year, he retired to Tiantong.
In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, he suddenly manifested a slight illness.
On the twelfth day, he passed away while sitting in the lotus posture.
He was sixty-nine years of age;
his dharma-age was fifty-two.
He was buried to the east of the monastery.
The Master responded to sentient beings according to their capacities,
his dignified demeanor being solemn and orderly.
By day, he sat upright with his robes adjusted to set an example for the assembly;
by night, he patrolled the hall, trimming the torches.
To awaken the delusions of the multitude,
he maintained his pure and white conduct until the end of his life without wavering.
His body was firm and solid,
remaining indestructible until death;
the teeth and hair he left behind produced many śarīras.
People considered this extraordinary.
The layman Zhang Yi, known as Yuezhai,
was a constant disciple who studied under the Master.
After the Master passed away, he further managed his subsequent affairs.
Among the dozens of others who succeeded him in the Dharma,
Liaowu Chongyue was particularly outstanding.
Bǐ served as an official in the capital city.
He met with his teacher there,
and they conversed together all day long.
He was indefatigable and forgot weariness.
After our parting, he frequently informed me by letter;
even as he approached his final passing, he again wrote a letter to bid me farewell.
After the burial had taken place,
the disciple Hui-guang, who was studying under him,
requested a commemorative inscription for the stupa.
His request for further instruction remained firm.
Thereupon, [the Master] composed an inscription for him, saying:
"A single drop from Caoxi— Its source is deep, its flow is long. Reaching Linji..."
His Way flourishes ever more: like sparks struck from stone, like flashes of lightning, it does not depart from the present moment;
one must directly encounter and accept it. How magnificent! This eminent master has entered the very hall itself;
his practice and realization are in accord—neither annihilation nor permanence.
Expounding with a single sound, seven times sitting at the site of enlightenment;
for the sickness and affliction of sentient beings, I am the King of Physicians. For sentient beings drowning in the sea, I am the ship and the helmsman.
Seated, I sever both the retribution and transformation bodies, without falling into confusion; all who hear me and see me—
Leaping and galloping forth, doubts were suddenly dispelled; Like leaves falling under frost, the ancestral wind did not decline.
Truly, the Master was a pillar and beam; His fame filled the world—how could it be hidden away?
